package.display_name: Melodia - room-aware dressing and game-ready level pipeline
package.scope: the P0 house leg (L_MelusinaHouse_P0) first, the pattern second

purpose: A scoped plan to make a Melodia room (a) placeable in one action, (b) dressable in a way that is aware of the room it sits in, (c) physically settled rather than posed, and (d) carry the gameplay loop. It also records the research and the shipped-game case studies the plan is built on.

authority.route: POITOU P0 Golden Walk house leg (M00-M05)
authority.note: This plan creates no new authority. Houdini keeps the room, PCG keeps the scatter, the dressing subsystem keeps the human art pass, and the artist keeps the gameplay.

meter.note: the same governing meter as the world canon: 0.6 m = 1 beat, 2.4 m = 1 bar of 4/4. The kit's standard doorway/bay system is built on it (see case study BS-04).

authority_rules: one writer per surface: Houdini writes the shell, PCG writes the fill, the dressing pass writes the art pass, the artist writes the interactables
nothing an agent or a script does may move, replace or delete a hand-placed actor; the fill is additive only
the fill never re-enters a kit's own materials: everything it spawns uses the converted M_Master_Toon_Universal instances
the art pass is editor-only by design and is never a shipping dependency; a shipping level gets baked or runtime-generated content, decided in W8
no second PCG authority, no second dressing authority, no new world compiler

case_studies.game: Fortnite (Unreal Editor for Fortnite) - Scene Graph, by Epic Games
case_studies.status: shipped platform, Scene Graph is Beta (Epic warns: use caution when shipping with it)
case_studies.mechanic: Levels are built as prefab assemblies. A prefab is a hierarchy of entities with components; the docs' own example builds 'two castle room prefabs' and then a castle and a village by swapping children. Geometry, sound cues and behaviour all live in the same reusable assembly, and each instance can override individual component values.
quotes: Anything you build in Scene Graph can be reused many times over, and with less memory.
You can quickly put together set pieces and game mechanics by harnessing the physical data from meshes, sound cues, and much more.
Editing prefabs doesn't affect the stability and memory of the original object or its copies.
steal: the room prefab as the unit of reuse - one assembly that carries geometry AND gameplay, which is exactly the 'BP that places geometry and carries the gameplay loop' the project needs
per-instance overrides as the artist's art-direction lever: change the floor in one room without touching the kit or the other instances
instancing for memory: the same reason PCG beats hand-placed actors
do_not_steal: Verse as the authoring language - the project already has C++ and Blueprints
Scene Graph itself: it is Beta, and the project must not add a platform-specific authoring authority

case_studies.mechanic: A reusable Blueprint Actor that generates complete rooms from splines: the spline defines the room, PCG samples it and spawns the contents.
quotes: This intermediate-to-advanced tutorial teaches you to create a reusable Blueprint Actor that automatically generates complete rooms from any ...

case_studies.game: THE FINALS (Embark Studios) - procedural buildings, by SideFX
case_studies.verified: listing confirmed 2026-10-22 (SideFX's article body is behind their site chrome; the quote is SideFX's own listing text)
case_studies.mechanic: A Houdini toolset that generates the game's buildings procedurally while keeping the artists in control of the result; the procedural structure then carries cover, traversal and combat space, and the art direction rides on top of it.
quotes: Houdini toolset that could automate the repetitive work while still giving artists creative control.
steal: the division of labour this project already chose: Houdini automates the repetitive shell work, the 33-parameter room shell is the artist's control surface, and gameplay is authored on top of the procedural structure
the reminder that procedural structure is where gameplay lives - the shell's openings and the medallion are beat geometry, not decoration
do_not_steal: full-building procedural generation: Melodia's house is an authored place with an authored route

case_studies.game: Bethesda open worlds (Oblivion, Fallout 3/4, Skyrim) - Joel Burgess, level designer, interviewed by 80 Level
case_studies.mechanic: Modular kits with a shared logic, a standard doorway system between kits, and a deliberate anti-repetition discipline.
quotes: Everyone knows that a kit-based level can look bland, and 'show the grid' in ways that make it obvious the environment is modular.
the better you can mix and match pieces within a kit and other kits in the game, the more combinations you can come up with to break up the monotony
One big saving grace in these kinds of games with many logically-distinct kits is to use a standard doorway system to connect them.
it's generally bad news to change certain aspects of a kit once levels are built with it. Things like pivot point location, base footprint size, and transition metrics can be a disaster
I think it's most critical to focus on functional polish early, and then allow for visual polish in the later stages of development.
steal: the standard doorway/bay system between room types - Melodia already has the meter (0.6 m module, 2.4 m bay); the room kit must expose one standard portal so a bedroom and a salon can be joined without bespoke geometry
FREEZE RULE: pivot, footprint and transition metrics are fixed before layout. A change after layout breaks every room that used the kit - so this becomes a durable rule in W4
the anti-repetition split: base layer (kit) + fill layer (scatter) + hero layer (the art pass) - three layers that mix so the grid does not show
functional polish first: the room must work before it is pretty, and the walk (W7) is the functional gate
do_not_steal: hard-binding a kit to one gameplay meaning: 'I generally stay away from hard associations between kits and certain gameplay or artistic decision' - the carrier is a swappable slot (W4), not a fixed child

case_studies.game: Unreal Engine 5 - Epic PCG Development Guides (reference)
case_studies.mechanic: The canonical reference for PCG graphs and their best-practice patterns (shape grammar, splines, filters, spawners).

research_notes: There is no native 'room' concept in this engine build's PCG plugin: no PCGRoomData, RoomLayout or PCGCreateRoom classes exist in the UE 5.8 PCG headers. Room-awareness therefore has to be built from splines + a bounds source + filters - which is what PCG_MelusinaRoomShell_PCGex already does. This kills the idea of 'use PCG Rooms' and justifies the spline approach in the fill contract.

The commercial tools this project modelled the Dash role on (Polygonflow Dash, Magpie) are absent and paid; the native subsystem is the fallback, and it must be built as a real implementation rather than left as the current scaffold.

BP_PhysicsSpawner does not exist in this repository, in Content or in git history. The capability it stood for - props that fall and settle - is the contract of UMelodiaDressingSubsystem::PhysicallyDrop, which is currently a scaffold. That is W2.

decisions.method: three independent samples; the mean distribution and the run-to-run agreement are the evidence, not a single draw

carrier_slot.meaning: the gameplay carrier is a FIXED CHILD of the room kit: dropping the room brings its interactable with it, so one action places a complete, playable room

density_paint.meaning: Jev could not separate paint-over-the-derived-pass (A) from paint-from-scratch (B) from use-as-is-then-repaint (C). This is the one question Jev has least to add to

mobility.meaning: keep the 82 movable dressing actors movable THROUGH the walk; the static conversion is a later pass, once the composition stops changing. Converting before the walk would fight the art pass

carrier_ownership.meaning: keep the borrowed Fab-pack carriers for the walk - they satisfy the beat contract today - and migrate to project-owned Blueprints in a later, separate pass

first_build.verdict: NEAR_TIE - W5 and W4 are effectively tied
first_build.meaning: build W5 (the fill graphs + the density paint) first: editor-side, no C++, and it is what shows the artist whether the pipeline is worth continuing. W4 (the room kit) is second

decisions.tension_to_watch: carrier_slot says the carrier is a fixed child of the kit, and carrier_ownership says the kit's default carrier stays a borrowed Fab-pack actor. Those combine into a kit whose default child is someone else's asset. If that reads wrong, option C on carrier_ownership (replace only the M02 resonant object with the project's token family) is the narrow fix that keeps the beat and keeps the loop mostly ours.
still_the_owners_call: density_paint: paint over the derived pass, paint from scratch, or use the derived field as-is for the first graph build and repaint after. Jev's spread is 0.33 / 0.37 / 0.27 - it has no answer to give.
whether the C++ work (W1/W2/W3) waits for a clean compile window - the owner answered 'def wait' on 2026-10-22.
decisions.packet_lesson: the first run of this packet sent criteria={option: None} - the option descriptions never reached the service, so it answered 'A' to all five questions with no confidence. The criteria TEXT must be transmitted. And this model's answer carries choice + confidence + a full probability distribution and NO reason field; a receipt that looks for .reason/.score records nulls that read as 'no confidence' when the confidence was there all along.
